note: Phase F step 7. Fixes the metrics and decision rules so a later reading cannot be reinterpreted after the fact.

disclosure_sample_size_was_visible.statement: The NUMBER of label-eligible days (39) was known when this contract was written, because it follows deterministically from the data horizon and the 20-day label. The IC values were not.
disclosure_sample_size_was_visible.consequence: The minimum of 40 labelled days sits just above the visible 39. A reader must be able to see that, and the rule must not be changed later to fit a future sample.
therefore: the threshold is recorded here as of this date and is not adjustable retroactively
the first reading is reported as EXPLORATORY by rule, not by judgement

observation_window.clean_window_justification: Data budget: development set 2023-06-01..2025-12-31 consumed; 2026-01-01..2026-07-17 permanently consumed by v6 M8. Clean data starts 2026-07-18, and 2026-07-20 is the first trading day with a complete forward bar.
observation_window.labelling_rule: A date is labelled only when its 20-trading-day forward window is fully inside the materialised panel. The last 20 trading days of any window are structurally unlabelled; this is a property of a forward label, not a data gap.

known_limitations.statement: Daily code count drops from about 3,132 before 2026-07-24 to about 2,633 after it (561 codes have no post-07-24 bars in the baostock backfill). B2 domain size falls from about 1,948 to about 1,590.
known_limitations.impact: Cross-day comparisons of domain size, turnover and concentration are not valid across the seam. Daily IC is a per-day cross-sectional statistic and is unaffected in construction, but the post-seam universe is a narrower, possibly non-random sample.
known_limitations.mitigation: Report every metric split by pre-seam (2026-07-20..07-24) and post-seam (2026-07-27..) sub-periods, and never present the post-seam domain as an investable universe.

known_limitations.statement: At most 39 labelled days exist today. A 20-day label on overlapping windows makes consecutive daily ICs strongly autocorrelated; effective independent samples are roughly 39/20, near 2.
known_limitations.impact: Any IC_IR computed here is essentially uninformative. A sign test on this sample has very low power.
known_limitations.mitigation: Interim readings below 40 labelled days are explicitly exploratory and cannot trigger promotion or rejection. HAC IC_IR is reported but is not a decision input before 250 days.

known_limitations.statement: The frozen panel industry column is a static snapshot. The SW2021 PIT alternative was measured on 2026-10-18: 156 codes genuinely reclassified, daily rank correlation 0.99181, bottom-decile overlap 0.9579.
known_limitations.impact: Neutralisation in the frozen scoring path uses the snapshot. This is a disclosed deviation, not an equivalence.
known_limitations.mitigation: Report industry exposure under both the snapshot and the PIT column; switching the production path requires a separate preregistration.

known_limitations.statement: benchmark 000985 after 2026-07-17 comes from a Tencent quote API extension, not the local archive. The fetched series reproduces the archive exactly on all 1,098 overlap days (max abs diff 0 on open/high/low/close).
known_limitations.impact: Label values after 2026-07-17 depend on a second source.
known_limitations.mitigation: The extension is verified before use and stored separately; the archive is never rewritten.

primary_endpoint.name: forward_daily_spearman_ic
primary_endpoint.definition: Per labelled date, Spearman rank correlation between prediction and y_excess20 over B2 members with both values present. Requires at least 500 names and at least 5 distinct values on each side, else the date is dropped and counted.

secondary_endpoints.name: forward_ic_win_rate
secondary_endpoints.definition: share of labelled dates with daily IC > 0

secondary_endpoints.name: forward_ic_hac_ir
secondary_endpoints.definition: mean IC divided by Newey-West long-run standard deviation, lag 20

secondary_endpoints.name: bottom_exclusion_list_turnover
secondary_endpoints.definition: Per date-to-date transition, |excluded_t intersect excluded_{t-1}| / |excluded_{t-1}| where excluded is the bottom 10% of the scored B2 cross-section.

secondary_endpoints.name: excluded_group_forward_excess
secondary_endpoints.definition: Mean y_excess20 of the bottom-10% excluded set minus mean y_excess20 of the full scored B2 cross-section, per labelled date, then averaged.

secondary_endpoints.name: industry_exposure_stability
secondary_endpoints.definition: Share of excluded names per industry, reported per date under the snapshot column and the SW2021 PIT column, plus the maximum single-industry share.

secondary_endpoints.name: score_distribution_drift
secondary_endpoints.definition: per-date mean and standard deviation of prediction over the scored B2 set

reference_values_from_frozen_evaluation.note: Evaluation period 2024-10-22..2025-12-31. Consumed; not a forward claim.

rule_all_of: both half-window IC means have the same sign as the full-window mean
PASS_CONTINUE.meaning: Forward behaviour is consistent with the frozen evaluation. Continue observing.

INCONCLUSIVE.rule: Does not satisfy PASS_CONTINUE and does not trigger any halt condition: positive but too small, sign-inconsistent between halves, or too few labelled days.
INCONCLUSIVE.meaning: Keep observing. No change to the frozen configuration is authorized.

rule_any_of: any day with fewer than 500 scored B2 names
more than 0.5% of predictions non-finite on any day
abs(mean_daily_spearman_ic) > 0.40 (implausible for a 20-day label; treat as leakage or bug, not alpha)
HALT.meaning: Stop and diagnose. A halt is not evidence against the factor; it means the observation environment is not trustworthy and must be explained before more data is collected.

forbidden_actions_during_observation: changing the label definition or horizon
using forward results to select factors
dropping days because their IC was unfavourable

requires: excluded_group_forward_excess negative and stable across halves
bottom_exclusion_list_turnover consistent with the historical C-track
promotion_gate.then: a separate preregistration for the v6 official lockbox, single unblinding

reporting.frequency: on demand, at least monthly while the window grows
must_report: labelled day count and dropped-day count
mean IC with and without the pre-seam days
excluded-group forward excess under both industry columns
explicit statement that the post-seam universe is narrower by 561 codes

turnover_consistency_operationalisation.why_now: The promotion gate required turnover to be consistent with the historical C-track but never said what consistent means. Fixing that after a formal reading would be discretionary, so it is fixed here, before one exists.

metric_definition.name: bottom_exclusion_membership_change_rate
metric_definition.warning: The keep rate (1 - change rate) is a different number. The forward run first reported 0.5267, which is the KEEP rate, next to the C-track 0.3805, which is the CHANGE rate. They must never be compared directly.

decision_rule.primary_metric: forward change rate versus the historical change rate RECOMPUTED at the forward tail size, by subsampling the historical tail to the same number of names and averaging over 50 random subsamples.
decision_rule.rationale: A rate difference that vanishes once the tail size is matched is an arithmetic artefact, not a change in scorer behaviour. Comparing raw rates across different domain sizes would fail a healthy scorer purely because the universe shrank.

current_status_under_this_rule.note: The 0.0023 absolute gap is far inside the 0.05 tolerance. On a like-for-like basis forward churn is indistinguishable from history.

invalidation_conditions: the forward tail size changes materially, so the matched baseline must be recomputed
the exclusion fraction changes (requires a new preregistration anyway)
the missing 558 codes are backfilled, which enlarges the tail and moves the rate down mechanically
turnover_consistency_operationalisation.explicit_boundary: This does NOT relax the promotion gate. It defines how the gate is measured. If the tail-size-matched comparison ever exceeds tolerance, the gate still fails.
